One No. 9 finish at Mexico City and it's done.

The youngest champion in history could be crowned Sunday. 🏆 #F1 #MexicoGP

x_posts.label: Post 1-2

2026 F1 standings heading into Mexico City:

1. Antonelli — 365 pts

A 123-point lead. Two points needed. This weekend, history gets made. #F1 #MexicoGP

facebook.long_form:
Posting Window: 8:00 AM ET

THE TITLE IS WITHIN REACH. 🏆

Kimi Antonelli arrives at the Mexico City Grand Prix just TWO POINTS away from the 2026 Formula 1 Drivers' Championship.

A No. 9 finish or better Sunday clinches it — regardless of what George Russell or Lewis Hamilton do. If neither of them wins the race, even a No. 10 finish would be enough.

Antonelli leads Russell by 123 points heading into Round 19 at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez: 365 to 242. He won the United States Grand Prix at COTA last weekend with a dominant drive that left nothing to chance.

The math is simple. The execution? That's where the drama lives.

Will Kimi Antonelli become the youngest Formula 1 World Champion in history this Sunday? Drop a 🏁 if you can't wait.

x_posts.label: Post 2-1

Sergio Pérez will start his 300th Formula 1 Grand Prix — at HOME in Mexico City.

From an F1 outsider to 300 starts. What a career. #MexicoGP #F1

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
Checo at 300 starts. In Mexico. In front of his home crowd.

Whatever happens Sunday, that number is remarkable. ❤️🇲🇽 #Perez #MexicoGP

facebook.long_form:
Posting Window: 10:00 AM ET

Sergio Pérez will line up on the Mexico City Grand Prix grid for the 300th time as a Formula 1 driver — and he's doing it at HOME.

From his debut as a relative unknown to 300 Grand Prix starts, Checo's career has been one of the most extraordinary journeys in modern motorsport. The retired talk was swirling in recent weeks, but Pérez played it down ahead of his milestone race, saying he has changed how he thinks about the scrutiny that comes with being an F1 driver and that he remains fully motivated.

300 starts. At home. In front of the Mexican fans who have cheered for him since the beginning.

Whatever Sunday holds, this is a number that deserves a moment.

Are you a Checo fan? Leave a 🇲🇽 in the comments.
facebook.image_caption: 300 F1 starts. At home in Mexico. Checo Pérez marks a milestone this Sunday. 🇲🇽 #F1 #Perez #MexicoGP

stories.title: Eight Teams Field Rookies in FP1 — Verstappen and Russell Sit Out Practice [TIER 2]

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
FP1 in Mexico City: 8 teams are handing their cars to rookies.

Iwasa (Red Bull), Vesti (Mercedes), Mini (Alpine), Herta (Cadillac) all get track time.

The future of F1 is on the track today. #F1 #MexicoGP

facebook.long_form:
Posting Window: 8:00 AM ET

Eight teams. Eight rookies. One extraordinary practice session.

FP1 at the Mexico City Grand Prix brings the most widespread rookie driver lineup of the season, with eight of the 10 F1 teams fielding non-regular drivers in the opening practice. It's the mandatory rookie session rule in full effect — and this time, the turnover is nearly universal.

Key substitutions:
🔴 Ayumu Iwasa steps into Max Verstappen's Red Bull
⚪ Frederik Vesti takes George Russell's Mercedes seat
🔵 Gabriele Mini gets his first F1 practice lap for Alpine, replacing Franco Colapinto
🔵 Colton Herta runs for Cadillac in a session with major implications (more on that shortly)

For fans who follow F1's next generation, this is appointment viewing. These are the drivers who may fill current seats in the coming seasons, and today's session gives them a taste of race-weekend conditions.

Which rookie are you most excited to watch? 👇
facebook.image_caption: Eight rookies. Eight teams. FP1 at Mexico City belongs to the next generation of F1. 🏎️ #F1 #MexicoGP

stories.title: Colton Herta's Last Shot at a Super License — Mexico FP1 His Final Chance [TIER 2]

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
Colton Herta's F1 future comes down to ONE practice session.

He needs 100 km in FP1 at Mexico City to earn the final super license point.

He missed at Monza. This is his last chance. 🇺🇸 #F1 #Cadillac

facebook.long_form:
Posting Window: 12:00 PM ET

Colton Herta's entire Formula 1 future could come down to ONE practice session this Friday.

The American driver needs to complete at least 100 kilometers in FP1 at Mexico City — without a penalty — to earn the final super license point that would make him eligible to race in F1 for Cadillac in 2027.

He tried this at Monza in September. A hydraulic failure cut his session short before he could cover the required distance. One cruel mechanical issue, one point lost, one dream delayed.

Mexico City is his last realistic chance this season. He needs 24 laps. Clean running. No incidents.

The stage is set. The stakes are enormous. Can Herta finally land the super license point that changes everything?

Follow along with us this Friday for live FP1 coverage. 🇺🇸
facebook.image_caption: Colton Herta needs 100 km in FP1 Friday. One clean session and his F1 dream moves closer. #F1 #Cadillac #MexicoGP

stories.title: Mexico City GP Preview — Altitude, Strategy, and Día de Muertos [TIER 2]

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Mexico City GP: 2,240 meters above sea level.

No F1 circuit puts more stress on engines, aero, and brakes.

Oh, and the title could be decided here Sunday. What a weekend ahead. 🇲🇽 #MexicoGP #F1

facebook.long_form:
Posting Window: 5:00 PM ET

The Mexico City Grand Prix is unlike any race on the F1 calendar — and this year, it could crown a world champion.

Here's what makes Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez so special:

🏔️ ALTITUDE: At 2,240 meters above sea level, Mexico City sits higher than almost any major motorsport venue in the world. The thin air reduces aerodynamic downforce, cuts engine power output, and demands more aggressive brake cooling strategies. Teams spend months of simulation time preparing for the specific conditions here.

🌬️ STRATEGY: With lower downforce efficiency, tire degradation behaves differently in Mexico than at most circuits. Teams often run higher wing angles than the numbers would suggest — the drag penalty is smaller when the air is thin — and pit windows can shift depending on how drivers manage their front tires through the quick Esses section.

🎃 DÍA DE MUERTOS: This year's race weekend coincides with one of Mexico's most iconic cultural celebrations. The atmosphere inside the stadium section of the circuit is electric at the best of times — during Día de Muertos, it becomes something else entirely.

And on Sunday, the 2026 world championship could be decided.

Which storyline are you most excited about this weekend? 🇲🇽👇
facebook.image_caption: 2,240 meters. Thin air. Día de Muertos. The title on the line. Mexico City is F1 at its most theatrical. 🇲🇽 #MexicoGP #F1
